from_the_bytes.decoder: pc 0 to 4293 (ok_permitBytes_decoded, any length): no value; call data of 164 bytes or more; clean address words; offset word <= 2^64 - 1; 4 + offset + 31 < size (signed); length word <= 2^64 - 1; 4 + offset + length + 32 <= size. Any failed check reverts, so in the theorems these are conclusions about a successful run, not hypotheses. 711 gas.
from_the_bytes.allocation_and_copy: the bytes are allocated at 128: length word at 128, free memory pointer = 128 + ((63 + ((L + 31) & ~31)) & ~31) = c + 160 with c = L rounded up to 32 (sigFree_W); CALLDATACOPY of exactly L bytes to 160, then a zero word at 160 + L; memory size c + 192. Gas copyCost c = 84 + 3 * (c / 32) + memoryGasCost (c + 192) - memoryGasCost 160 (bytes_copy_any, exact).
from_the_bytes.length_check: at pc 2704.. the code compares the length word with 65 (sub 65 L). Only L = 65 takes the ECRECOVER path. Every other L (0, 1..64, 66.., up to 2^64 - 1) jumps to the EXTCODESIZE of the owner (pc 3580): owner with no code reverts, else isValidSignature by STATICCALL.
from_the_bytes.encoder: free memory pointer F (c + 482 on chain id 1, c + 802 else, F % 32 = 2 because the digest preimage of 66 bytes was allocated without rounding). The code writes the digest, 64 and L at F + 36, copies the signature with the routine at pc 3812 (32 bytes per turn, ceil(L/32) turns, then a zero word at the end) to F + 132, writes the selector over F + 32, then copies the c + 100 bytes of the call data once more to F + c + 132 and calls with input (F + c + 132, c + 100) and output (F + 2c + 232, 32). Memory ends at F + 2c + 286. Gas encCost F c = 841 + 134 * (c / 32) + memoryGasCost (F + 2c + 286) - memoryGasCost (F + 30) (encoder, exact).
from_the_bytes.call_data: erc1271Bytes digest sig = 0x1626ba7e ++ digest ++ 64 ++ L ++ sig ++ zeros to the next multiple of 32: 100 + ceil32(L) bytes (enc_chain proves the memory at the call arguments is exactly this, for the L bytes copied from the call data).

cases.n = 0: c = 0, nothing copied, call data of 100 bytes with length 0; same theorems
cases.n < 65 and n > 65: same path, same theorems (length is a variable)
cases.very large n: bounded by the decoder at 2^64 - 1 and by the call data size (bytesIn); the theorems hold for every such L; memory cost grows with c^2 so a real run ends out of gas long before, which is an error and not a successful run
cases.malformed offset or length: the decoder reverts (offset > 2^64 - 1, length word outside the call data, length > 2^64 - 1, bytes outside the call data); no hypothesis on the offset word is used
cases.dirty padding after the bytes: not read: the code copies L bytes and writes its own zeros
